programme.displayName: Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test
programme.subtitle: SAA-C03 Amazon SQS hands-on lab catalogue
programme.description: A beginner-friendly catalogue of hands-on Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) labs for AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) preparation. This replacement preserves the programme identity while expanding its scope from a single queue test into a staged SQS learning path.
programme.learningOutcome: Plan and complete beginner-friendly Amazon SQS labs that progress from basic queue operations to SAA-C03 architecture patterns.

tasks.title: 1. Create an IAM User for the SQS Labs
tasks.goal: Create a console-only IAM lab user named sqs-lab-user, explain why routine SQS work should not use the root user, and verify that an administrator has granted the user the minimum approved access needed for the selected lab.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 expects secure identity choices. IAM users have no permissions by default; AWS recommends federation for human users where possible and limiting root-user use to tasks that require it.

tasks.goal: Sign in using the approved lab identity, open Amazon SQS, select Europe (London) eu-west-2, and confirm that permitted queue actions are visible.
tasks.whyItMatters: SQS is regional. SAA-C03 scenarios often depend on choosing regional resources consistently and diagnosing an authorization failure separately from a missing resource.

tasks.title: 3. Create a Standard Queue and Record Its Queue URL
tasks.goal: Create a harmless standard queue, identify its queue URL and ARN, and distinguish the queue URL used by API operations from the queue name.
tasks.whyItMatters: Queue URLs are required by many SQS operations. Standard queues are the default SAA-C03 choice when maximum throughput and loose ordering are acceptable.

tasks.title: 4. Send, Receive, Inspect, and Delete a Standard-Queue Message
tasks.goal: Send harmless sample text, inspect its message ID and receive count, receive it, and explicitly delete it using the receipt handle workflow.
tasks.whyItMatters: This is the essential SQS lifecycle: sending is separate from consuming, and receiving alone does not permanently remove a message.

tasks.title: 5. Receive Without Deleting and Observe Visibility Timeout
tasks.goal: Receive a message without deleting it, observe that it becomes temporarily invisible, and observe it become available again after the configured visibility timeout.
tasks.whyItMatters: A visibility timeout protects work in progress but does not guarantee exactly-once processing for a standard queue.

findings.message: The request says to stop after a numbered master catalogue, while the supplied Follow Along contract requests full Console and CLI procedures for every task. This replacement therefore provides the approved catalogue structure only; detailed task procedures, test scripts, cleanup, and architecture walkthroughs remain deferred.

The requested first lab asks to create or attach least-privilege SQS permissions. The protected authoring instruction prohibits proposing an IAM policy. A detailed revision must therefore either reference an organization-approved permission set administered outside the Follow Along or receive an explicit exception allowing policy content.

The catalogue is incomplete because the response contract limits the practical size of a complete replacement package. Remaining planned catalogue entries to add in the next approved revision are: FIFO MessageGroupId ordering; deduplication IDs and content-based deduplication; Standard versus FIFO comparison; DLQs, maxReceiveCount, forced failures, DLQ inspection, and redrive; producer-worker decoupling and buffering spikes; message attributes; S3 large-payload pointer pattern; SSE and KMS; queue policies, service permissions, cross-account SQS, and permission-failure diagnosis; Lambda event-source mappings, batch size, partial batch failures, retries, and serverless processing; SNS-to-SQS fan-out; S3-to-SQS notifications; EventBridge-to-SQS routing; EC2 worker consumers; CloudWatch SQS metrics and alarms; backlog-driven Auto Scaling; SQS versus SNS, EventBridge, Kinesis, direct Lambda invocation, and direct backend processing; and SAA-C03 scenario labs for traffic spikes, slow backends, failed orders, strict ordering, fan-out, worker crashes, serverless processing, and Auto Scaling.

The current published programme identity is preserved: programme ID sqs-learning-path, display name Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test, service Amazon Simple Queue Service, short name SQS, and published source revision 2.
